items.title: 52222_Marshall Royal oral history interview
items.q: everybody thought in the big ways, like Louis B. Mayer

ctx.x: You told me off the tape, not on the tape, about how you happened to work with Duke in 1930 in "Check and Double Check."

Yeah, well, that was one of the ironies of big business. When the people brought Duke Ellington out here to do the music and to work in "Check and Double Check," all they were thinking about was the extravaganzas of movies and everybody thought in the big ways, like Louis B. Mayer, if

he was going to do a picture, he didn't think it would be correct unless they had at least 50 people doing the music behind the scenes and as long as it was big, a lot of times they figures big was good. So when Ellington came out here with about 12 pieces or however many people in his band, well, immediately, the people that were running the show out there -- I can't think of the name of the company.
